Consider the line shown above, which has a slope of $2.$ The equation of the line is $y=${{field-1}}
$x\,+$

question.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b.$ We know that the slope is $m=2,$ so we just need to work out $y$-intercept $b.$

From the graph, we see that the line passes through the point $(1,5).$ Substituting this into $y=mx+b$ with $m=2$ and solving for $b,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =2x+b \\ 5 & =2(1)+b \\ 5 & =2+b \\ b & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is $y=2x+3.$
